title: Convey, even one verse
hook: convey from me, even one verse, and in the same breath, don't lie about me
tomorrow: what made one teacher keep his seat in the mosque?

segments.voice: Yesterday: service is prayer, the same box carried with a different why. A new stretch starts today: passing it on.

Someone posts a verse over a photo of a sunset. Someone else replies: you're not a scholar, stay in your lane. Who's right? Do you have to be an expert before you share? One short hadith seems to answer at once. Then, in the very same breath, it adds a warning, and people still weigh the two halves.
screen: `A VERSE OVER A SUNSET.` → `STAY IN YOUR LANE?` → `ONE HADITH, TWO HALVES.`

segments.voice: It's in Sahih al-Bukhari. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: convey from me, even if it's one aya, one verse. And at the end of the same hadith: whoever lies about me on purpose, let him take his seat in the Fire. Two halves. Each has its defenders. One view leans on the first half. Even one verse. You don't need a degree to pass on what you've truly learned. The Prophet asked for it, and he set the bar low: one verse. A community where only experts speak goes quiet. At its best, this side says: knowledge that isn't shared dies with the person who holds it. The other view leans on the second half. The Qur'an says, in Pickthall's words: "follow not that whereof thou hast no knowledge." Passing on a hadith you half-remember, or an explanation you made up on the spot, isn't humility. It can put words in the Prophet's mouth. At its best, this side says: a wrong word travels faster than a right one, and it's hard to call back. The hadith itself keeps both halves in one breath. Share. Don't invent.
screen: `CONVEY FROM ME, EVEN ONE VERSE.` · `DON'T LIE ABOUT ME.` · `SIDE ONE: UNSHARED, IT DIES.` · `SIDE TWO: A WRONG WORD SPREADS.` · then, large: `EVEN ONE VERSE.`

segments.voice: Choose one line you know well and trust: a verse, a short surah, even just bismillah. Check that you have it exactly, then say it once, slowly, out loud. Let it sit in the quiet after.
screen: `ONE LINE YOU TRUST.` · `EXACTLY AS IT IS.` · `SAY IT ONCE, SLOWLY.`

segments.voice: Convey: to pass on what you've received. In the hadith, even one verse is enough to count, as long as it's passed on true.
Pocket this: even one verse, as long as it's the real one. Catch you tomorrow.

fork.setup: you lean toward the sharing side: everyone should pass on what they know. what's the strongest case for the careful side?
options: a wrong word about the Prophet spreads fast and is hard to call back.

fork.reveal: the careful side rests on the hadith's own second half and on 17:36: don't follow what you don't know. it isn't against sharing; it's against inventing.
